answer.worked:
The shaded region changes upper boundary at the lower intersection.
$$\begin{aligned}x&=2(x-3)^2\\0&=2x^2-13x+18\\0&=(2x-9)(x-2)\\x&=2,\ \frac92\end{aligned}$$
Use $x=2$ for the shaded region.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_0^2 x\,dx+\int_2^3 2(x-3)^2\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^2+\left[\frac{2(x-3)^3}{3}\right]_2^3\\&=(2-0)+\left(0-\left(-\frac23\right)\right)\\&=\frac83\ \mathrm{u}^2\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
Intersection points:
$$\begin{aligned}x^2-3x&=3-x\\x^2-2x-3&=0\\(x-3)(x+1)&=0\\x&=-1,3\end{aligned}$$
In the required region, $y=3-x$ is the upper curve.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_{-1}^{3}\big((3-x)-(x^2-3x)\big)\,dx\\&=\int_{-1}^{3}(3+2x-x^2)\,dx\\&=\left[3x+x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{3}\\&=9-\left(-\frac53\right)\\&=\frac{32}{3}\text{ u}^2\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: Find the area bounded between $y=x(x-4)^2$ and $y=x$.

spec.description: Black cubic and increasing line, arrowed axes and curve ends, no ticks or numerical labels. Both bounded regions are shaded with the house light green.
spec.mathematics: The curves y=x(x-4)^2 and y=x intersect at x=0,3,5. Shade between them on [0,3] and [3,5]; the cubic touches the x-axis at x=4.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied shaded graph is permanently visible; intersection values and calculated areas are answer-only.

answer.worked:
The intersections satisfy
$$\begin{aligned}x(x-4)^2&=x\\x\big((x-4)^2-1\big)&=0\\x(x-3)(x-5)&=0\\x&=0,3,5.\end{aligned}$$
The cubic is above the line on $0<x<3$; the line is above the cubic on $3<x<5$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_0^3\big(x(x-4)^2-x\big)\,dx+\int_3^5\big(x-x(x-4)^2\big)\,dx\\&=\int_0^3(x^3-8x^2+15x)\,dx-\int_3^5(x^3-8x^2+15x)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{8x^3}{3}+\frac{15x^2}{2}\right]_0^3-\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{8x^3}{3}+\frac{15x^2}{2}\right]_3^5\\&=\left(\frac{63}{4}-0\right)-\left(\frac{125}{12}-\frac{63}{4}\right)\\&=\frac{63}{4}+\frac{16}{3}\\&=\frac{253}{12}\text{ units}^2.\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: Find the area bounded between $y=6-2x$ and $y=x(x-3)^2$.

spec.description: Black cubic and descending line, arrowed axes and curve ends, no ticks or numerical labels. The two narrow bounded regions are shaded with the house light green.

spec.answerVisibility: The supplied shaded graph is permanently visible; intersection values and calculated areas are answer-only.

answer.worked:
The intersections satisfy
$$\begin{aligned}x(x-3)^2&=6-2x\\x^3-6x^2+11x-6&=0\\(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)&=0\\x&=1,2,3.\end{aligned}$$
The cubic is above the line on $1<x<2$; the line is above the cubic on $2<x<3$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_1^2\big(x(x-3)^2-(6-2x)\big)\,dx+\int_2^3\big((6-2x)-x(x-3)^2\big)\,dx\\&=\int_1^2(x^3-6x^2+11x-6)\,dx-\int_2^3(x^3-6x^2+11x-6)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-2x^3+\frac{11x^2}{2}-6x\right]_1^2-\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-2x^3+\frac{11x^2}{2}-6x\right]_2^3\\&=\left(-2+\frac94\right)-\left(-\frac94+2\right)\\&=\frac14+\frac14\\&=\frac12\text{ units}^2.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
At the intersections,
$$\begin{aligned}y^2&=2y\\y(y-2)&=0\\y&=0,2.\end{aligned}$$
For $0<y<2$, the right curve is $x=2y$ and the left curve is $x=y^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_0^2(2y-y^2)\,dy\\&=\left[y^2-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_0^2\\&=4-\frac83\\&=\frac43\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.mathematics: x=y^2 and x=3y-2; intersections (1,1) and (4,2).

answer.worked:
At the intersections,
$$\begin{aligned}y^2&=3y-2\\y^2-3y+2&=0\\(y-1)(y-2)&=0\\y&=1,2.\end{aligned}$$
For $1<y<2$, the right curve is $x=3y-2$ and the left curve is $x=y^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_1^2(3y-2-y^2)\,dy\\&=\left[\frac{3y^2}{2}-2y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_1^2\\&=\left(-\frac23\right)-\left(-\frac56\right)\\&=\frac16\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
At the intersections,
$$\begin{aligned}5y-y^2-4&=4-y\\y^2-6y+8&=0\\(y-2)(y-4)&=0\\y&=2,4.\end{aligned}$$
For $2<y<4$, the parabola is the right boundary and the line is the left boundary.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_2^4\big[(5y-y^2-4)-(4-y)\big]\,dy\\&=\int_2^4(6y-y^2-8)\,dy\\&=\left[3y^2-\frac{y^3}{3}-8y\right]_2^4\\&=-\frac{16}{3}-\left(-\frac{20}{3}\right)\\&=\frac43\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$

For $-1<y<2$, the line is the right boundary and the parabola is the left boundary.

For $0<x<\frac12$, $f(x)<g(x)$, so the second curve is above the first.

For $\frac12<x<1$, $f(x)>g(x)$, so the first curve is above the second.

Reflection in $x=\frac12$ interchanges the curves, so the two regions have equal area.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=2\int_{0}^{1/2}\left[x(1-x)^{2}-x^{2}(1-x)\right]\,dx\\A&=2\int_{0}^{1/2}x(1-x)(1-2x)\,dx\\A&=2\int_{0}^{1/2}(x-3x^{2}+2x^{3})\,dx\\A&=2\left[\frac{x^{2}}2-x^{3}+\frac{x^{4}}2\right]_{0}^{1/2}\\A&=2\left(\frac18-\frac18+\frac1{32}\right)\\A&=\frac1{16}\text{ units}^{2}.\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: Show that the $x$-coordinate of $A$ is $\dfrac{4}{a+1}$.

answer.short: Equating the curves gives $x\big((a+1)x-4\big)=0$, so $x=0$ or $x=\dfrac{4}{a+1}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}4x-x^2&=ax^2\\(a+1)x^2-4x&=0\\x\big((a+1)x-4\big)&=0\end{align*}$$
So $x=0$ (the origin $O$) or $x=\dfrac{4}{a+1}$, which is the $x$-coordinate of $A$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the value of $a$ such that the shaded area is $\dfrac{16}{3}$.

answer.short: Area $=\dfrac{32}{3(a+1)^2}$. Setting this equal to $\dfrac{16}{3}$ gives $(a+1)^2=2$, so $a=\sqrt2-1$.
answer.worked:
The shaded region lies between $x=0$ and $x=\frac{4}{a+1}$, with $y=4x-x^2$ above $y=ax^2$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=\int_0^{\frac{4}{a+1}}\left(4x-(a+1)x^2\right)dx\\&=\left[2x^2-\frac{(a+1)x^3}{3}\right]_0^{\frac{4}{a+1}}\\&=\frac{32}{(a+1)^2}-\frac{64}{3(a+1)^2}\\&=\frac{32}{3(a+1)^2}\end{align*}$$
Set the area equal to $\frac{16}{3}$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{32}{3(a+1)^2}&=\frac{16}{3}\\(a+1)^2&=2\end{align*}$$
Since $a>0$, $a+1>0$, so $a+1=\sqrt2$ and $a=\sqrt2-1$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: By considering the value of $\theta$, find the exact area of the shaded region, as shown on the diagram.

answer.short: $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$; shaded area $=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac12$ square units (sector minus triangle).
answer.worked:
The point $(1,1)$ gives $\tan\theta=\frac11=1$, so $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$. The radius is $r=\sqrt2$.
The shaded region is the sector with angle $\theta$ minus the right triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Sector}&=\frac12r^2\theta=\frac12(2)\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{4}\\\text{Triangle}&=\frac12(1)(1)=\frac12\\\text{Shaded area}&=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b

answer.worked:
Substitute $(0,0)$ (note $b\neq0$):
$$\begin{align*}0&=\frac{a}{b}-1\\a&=b\end{align*}$$
Substitute $(1,1)$ and use $a=b$:
$$\begin{align*}1&=\frac{a}{b-1}-1\\2&=\frac{a}{a-1}\\2a-2&=a\\a&=2\end{align*}$$
Hence $a=b=2$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Using parts (a) and (b), find the exact area of the region bounded by the hyperbola, the positive $x$-axis and the circle as shown on the diagram.

answer.short: $2\ln2+\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac32$ square units: the area under the hyperbola on $[0,1]$ plus the circular piece from part (a).
answer.worked:
With $a=b=2$ the hyperbola is $y=\frac{2}{2-x}-1$. The required region is the area under the hyperbola for $0\le x\le1$ together with the circular piece to the right of $x=1$ from part (a).
$$\begin{align*}\int_0^1\left(\frac{2}{2-x}-1\right)dx&=\Big[-2\ln(2-x)-x\Big]_0^1\\&=(0-1)-(-2\ln2)\\&=2\ln2-1\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total area}&=(2\ln2-1)+\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12\right)\\&=2\ln2+\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac32\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

Let f(x) = x²(1 − x) and g(x) = x(1 − x)²
f(x) − g(x) = x(1 − x)(x − (1 − x)) = x(1 − x)(2x − 1)
On [0, 1/2]: (2x − 1) < 0, so f < g (second curve above)
On [1/2, 1]: (2x − 1) > 0, so f > g (first curve above)
By symmetry, both regions have equal area.

= 2∫₀^(1/2) x(1 − x)(1 − 2x) dx
= 2∫₀^(1/2) (x − 3x² + 2x³) dx
= 2[x²/2 − x³ + x⁴/2]₀^(1/2)
= 2(1/8 − 1/8 + 1/32)
= 1/16 u²
